description: Add a fourth rank-averaged member: an MLP (256,64, early stopping) on quantile-normal-scaled features, averaged over three seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) before ranking, with all other features and members unchanged.

Add balanced class weighting to the RF (balanced_subsample), LightGBM (balanced) and CatBoost (auto_class_weights='Balanced') members, leaving features, other hyperparameters and rank-averaging unchanged.

Change the CatBoost member to depth 8, learning_rate 0.03, 800 iterations and l2_leaf_reg 5 (rsm, thread_count and seed unchanged) to test a deeper but more regularized booster inside the existing rank-average ensemble.

Adds one round of transductive pseudo-labelling on top of the standardized, kNN and MLP ensemble: confident test molecules (averaged probability above 0.9 or below 0.1, capped at 40% of the test set) are added with weight 0.3 and all members are refit before the final rank average.

The job timed out because fit_predict runs the full ensemble twice (a second pseudo-labelling pass), and the 15 fits together exceed 600 s. The fix drops the second pass so each fit trains the ensemble once.

Make the LightGBM member use extra_trees=True, min_child_samples=10, reg_lambda=1.0 and 500 estimators (learning_rate 0.05, other settings unchanged) to add regularization on the descriptor and fingerprint columns.

Add a standardized-molecule (largest fragment plus uncharging, with fallback), a multi-k Tanimoto similarity committee (k=5/25/100 on binary Morgan bits, rank-averaged) and a quantile-scaled MLP (256,64) as rank-averaged ensemble members alongside RF, LightGBM and CatBoost.

issues: No measurement circumvention found: no file or network access, no pasted answers, and no use of test labels. The kNN committee indexes y[idx] where idx points into training rows only; test SMILES are used as features, which fit_predict allows.

Column-order assumption: the kNN block treats X[:, -N_BITS:] as the Morgan count fingerprint. Correct only if featurize concatenates descriptors before the fingerprint. If reversed, the similarity committee runs on descriptor columns. That would add noise, not leak, so the result stays meaningful, but the order in featurize should be confirmed.
y[idx] fancy-indexing requires y to be a numpy array; a plain list would raise. Both candidate runs returned numbers, so this holds in practice, but it is an implicit assumption.
Added cost: a dense len(test) x len(train) similarity matrix plus an MLP on ~2250 features. Fine at n=1624 and well inside the 6 GB / 10 min limits, but memory grows quadratically with dataset size.

Recomputed z = 1.091 (candidate mean 0.08765 over 2 runs; incumbent 0.0942 over 1 run; difference 0.00655; SE = 0.0049*sqrt(1/2 + 1/1) = 0.00600). Agrees with the reported z = 1.088 and supports the provisional reject.

Complexity note against 'simpler is better': the diff bundles three independent changes (standardization, Tanimoto committee, MLP member). With an insignificant z, the added code is not yet justified and the components have not been attributed individually.

description: Add a standardized-molecule (largest fragment plus uncharging, with fallback), a multi-k Tanimoto similarity committee (k=5/25/100 on binary Morgan bits, rank-averaged) and a quantile-scaled MLP (256,64) as rank-averaged ensemble members alongside RF, LightGBM and CatBoost.

Standardize molecules (largest fragment plus neutralization, with fallback), add a Tanimoto kNN and a quantile-scaled MLP as rank-averaged members, and seed-bag the RF/LightGBM/CatBoost/MLP members over three derived seeds with the kNN run once.

Descriptor noise augmentation: the training set is tripled by adding two copies of each row with Gaussian noise (sd 0.05 times each descriptor column's training std) on the RDKit descriptor columns only, leaving Morgan counts and labels unchanged, using a seeded numpy Generator.

Adds an SVD-compressed view for the MLP member: after standardizing molecules (largest fragment plus neutralization, with fallback) and adding the Tanimoto kNN and MLP members, the MLP is fit on QuantileTransformer-scaled RDKit descriptors concatenated with 128 TruncatedSVD components of the Morgan count matrix, while RF, LightGBM, CatBoost and kNN keep their original inputs.

issues: Recomputed z = 1.93 (diff 0.0942 - 0.08265 = 0.01155; SE = 0.0049*sqrt(1/2 + 1/1) = 0.0060), consistent with the reported 1.915; still only 2 candidate runs vs 1 incumbent run, so the margin is thin relative to the 0.0049 noise sd.

Fit/transform discipline looks correct: QuantileTransformer, TruncatedSVD and all models are fit on training rows only; the kNN block uses train labels only and test molecules contribute just similarity values.

Robustness: standardize() returns Chem.MolFromSmiles(smi) which is None for an unparseable SMILES, and the descriptor loop would then raise. The incumbent had the same exposure, so this is not a new defect, but it is a crash risk on the final full-data fit.

Complexity cost: the diff adds standardization, a Tanimoto kNN, SVD+quantile features and an MLP all at once, so the per-component contribution is unknown and the added runtime is unmeasured against the 10-minute cap.
Ensemble members are averaged with equal rank weights, so the newly added kNN and MLP each get the same weight as the tree models without any validation evidence that this is the right split.

description: Adds an SVD-compressed view for the MLP member: after standardizing molecules (largest fragment plus neutralization, with fallback) and adding the Tanimoto kNN and MLP members, the MLP is fit on QuantileTransformer-scaled RDKit descriptors concatenated with 128 TruncatedSVD components of the Morgan count matrix, while RF, LightGBM, CatBoost and kNN keep their original inputs.

Add one round of transductive pseudo-labelling inside fit_predict: confident test molecules (rank score above 0.90 or below 0.10, capped at 30% of the test set, most extreme first) are added to the training data with sample_weight 0.3, the three-member rank-average ensemble is refit, and its test predictions are returned.

Add a precomputed-kernel KernelRidge member (0.5 MinMax-Tanimoto on Morgan counts + 0.5 RBF on standardized descriptors, alpha picked from {0.1, 1.0} by scaffold-grouped 3-fold inner AUROC) as a sixth rank-averaged member, on top of the standardized-molecule featurization and the Tanimoto kNN and quantile-MLP members.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access and no hardcoded answers. Test labels are never used. The test SMILES are used only for unsupervised features (Tanimoto similarity to training molecules, transform() of a QuantileTransformer fitted on train, descriptor scaling with train mean and sd), which is legitimate.
The inner GroupKFold used to choose alpha for KernelRidge uses only training data and scaffold groups. No leakage.

Unverified assumption: the code takes descriptor columns as X[:, :nd] and fingerprint columns as X[:, nd:]. The diff does not show the concatenation order in featurize; fp is computed before desc in the loop. If the order is actually [fp, desc], the kernel and kNN members get the wrong blocks. That would hurt performance but would not make the measured loss invalid. Please check.

Recomputed z: candidate mean (0.0873 + 0.0822) / 2 = 0.08475. Difference from the incumbent = 0.00945. SE = 0.0049 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/1) = 0.0060, so z ≈ 1.57. This matches the harness's 1.566; the small gap is from rounding.
Borderline evidence: the incumbent has only 1 run and z ≈ 1.57. One more incumbent or candidate replicate would make the decision firmer.

The diff bundles several changes: standardization/uncharging (which changes the features of every existing model), kNN, MLP, and KernelRidge with a scaffold-CV alpha search. The gains can't be attributed to any one part, and about 60 lines is a lot of code under the 'simpler is better' rule. An ablation is worth doing later.

Runtime risk: minmax_tanimoto loops over rows with 2048-dim count vectors (O(n^2 * 2048) per fit), plus the MLP and an inner CV across 15 fits. The job finished, but it is likely close to the 10-minute limit. Wall time is not reported.
standardize() returns None for unparseable SMILES, the same as before. Behaviour is unchanged.

description: Add a precomputed-kernel KernelRidge member (0.5 MinMax-Tanimoto on Morgan counts + 0.5 RBF on standardized descriptors, alpha picked from {0.1, 1.0} by scaffold-grouped 3-fold inner AUROC) as a sixth rank-averaged member, on top of the standardized-molecule featurization and the Tanimoto kNN and quantile-MLP members.

Standardize molecules (largest fragment, neutralization, fallback to the original) and replace the radius-2 Morgan block with concatenated radius 1, 2 and 3 count fingerprints (2048 bits each), adding a Tanimoto kNN (k=15) on binary radius-2 bits and a QuantileTransformer+MLP(256,64) as two more rank-averaged members.

issues: No measurement-evasion found: no file/network access, no pasted answers, no use of test labels. The Tanimoto kNN uses only train labels (ytr); test molecules contribute fingerprints only. QuantileTransformer is fit on train and merely applied to test; MLP early stopping splits the training set only.

Runtime risk (not a bug): three Morgan generators (radii 1,2,3), the full Descriptors list, a dense Tanimoto similarity matrix, and an MLP on ~6k+ features per fold is a large cost increase over the incumbent's 33 s; headroom against the 10-minute wall for 15 fits should be confirmed.
Minor robustness: standardize() returns None if Chem.MolFromSmiles fails, which would raise in the descriptor comprehension; the incumbent had the same exposure, so no regression.
Minor: tanimoto_knn relies on n_train > K_NN=15 for argpartition, which holds at these fold sizes.
Evidence is thin on the incumbent side: 2 candidate runs vs 1 incumbent run, so z rests on a single incumbent measurement.

description: Standardize molecules (largest fragment, neutralization, fallback to the original) and replace the radius-2 Morgan block with concatenated radius 1, 2 and 3 count fingerprints (2048 bits each), adding a Tanimoto kNN (k=15) on binary radius-2 bits and a QuantileTransformer+MLP(256,64) as two more rank-averaged members.

Adds Gaussian descriptor-noise augmentation (two noisy copies at 0.05x column sd, tree/boosting/MLP members only) on top of the standardization plus kNN and MLP base, with CatBoost kept at 500 iterations.

issues: No measurement circumvention found: no file or network access, no pasted predictions, and test labels are never touched. The kNN uses only train labels, QuantileTransformer is fit on train X only, and augmentation is applied only to training rows.

No validity-breaking bug. standardize() falls back to the raw molecule on failure, so parse behaviour matches the incumbent. argpartition with k=15 is safe since each training fold has far more than 15 molecules.

Minor: MLPClassifier early_stopping takes its validation split from the augmented matrix Xa, so near-duplicate noisy copies of the same molecule can appear on both sides of that split. Early stopping is therefore optimistic and the MLP likely trains longer than ideal. This affects only the internal stopping rule, not the reported harness score.

Verify feature layout: augment() treats columns [:N_DESC] as descriptors while tanimoto_knn treats [N_DESC:] as fingerprint bits. Both are consistent with a [descriptors, fingerprint] concatenation; if featurize concatenates fingerprint first, both components would be silently wrong (noise on counts, binarized descriptors for Tanimoto). The diff does not show the concatenation line, so this should be confirmed in the file.

Runtime risk worth noting: augmentation triples the training rows for the RF/LGBM/CatBoost ensemble and adds an MLP, against a 10-minute cap for 15 fits. The two completed runs imply it fits, but headroom is reduced.

Recomputed z = 1.94 from the stated numbers, matching the harness. Candidate mean 0.08255 vs incumbent 0.0942, difference 0.01165, SE = sqrt((0.0049/sqrt(2))^2 + 0.0049^2) = 0.0060. With only 2 candidate runs and 1 incumbent run this sits just under a 2-sigma threshold, so the accept is genuinely borderline rather than well-established.

description: Adds Gaussian descriptor-noise augmentation (two noisy copies at 0.05x column sd, tree/boosting/MLP members only) on top of the standardization plus kNN and MLP base, with CatBoost kept at 500 iterations.

Replace the single radius-2 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprint with radius-1 and radius-3 2048-bit Morgan count blocks concatenated after the RDKit descriptors, keeping the three-model rank-average ensemble unchanged.

Standardize molecules (largest fragment, then neutralize, falling back to the parsed molecule on error), then add a Tanimoto-weighted kNN (k=15) on binary Morgan bits and an MLP on quantile-normal features as two more rank-averaged members alongside RF, LightGBM and CatBoost, to get a second measurement of this consolidated configuration.

Standardize molecules (largest fragment, then neutralize, falling back to the parsed molecule on error), then add a Tanimoto-weighted kNN (k=15) on binary Morgan bits and an MLP on quantile-normal features as two more rank-averaged members alongside RF, LightGBM and CatBoost, to get a second measurement of this consolidated configuration.

Augment the training set with two jittered copies whose descriptor columns get Gaussian noise at 0.05 times each column's training sd (seeded by the seed argument), so RF, LightGBM and CatBoost fit on 3x rows, with the same rank-average for the untouched test matrix.
Append a 1024-bit Avalon count fingerprint to the descriptor and Morgan count features used by the rank-averaged RF/LightGBM/CatBoost ensemble.

Add balanced class weighting to the three ensemble members (class_weight='balanced_subsample' for the random forest, is_unbalance=True for LightGBM, auto_class_weights='Balanced' for CatBoost), leaving everything else unchanged.

Standardize molecules (largest fragment plus neutralization, with fallback), then replace the equal-weight rank average of RF, LightGBM, CatBoost, Tanimoto kNN (k=15) and MLP with weights chosen by scaffold-grouped inner 5-fold OOF AUROC over corners, equal pairs/triples and the uniform blend, shrunk halfway toward uniform.

issues: Recomputed z ~1.53 (diff 0.0092, SE = 0.0049*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.0060), matching the reported 1.528; this is below a conventional 1.96 bar and the incumbent has only 1 run, so the 'accept' is weakly supported. An extra incumbent replicate would firm it up.

Complexity cost is large relative to the gain: 5 member models, an inner scaffold-grouped GroupKFold, and a combinatorial weight search replace a 3-model average. The brief says a small gain is not worth ugly code.

Runtime risk: each fit_predict now trains 5 members x 5 inner folds plus 5 full-data fits (MLP and CatBoost included), a large increase over the ~33 s baseline. It evidently fit inside the 10-minute cap for these runs, but there is little headroom, and the final all-data fit is not covered by the CV timing.

Possible column-slicing bug worth confirming: fit_member slices X[:, N_DESC:] for the kNN fingerprint block, which is only correct if featurize concatenates descriptors before the fingerprint. The concatenation line is not shown in the diff. If the order is (fp, desc) the kNN member silently uses the wrong columns. This would weaken one member rather than invalidate the measurement, so it is not a veto, but it should be checked.

choose_weights selects over 5 singletons + 20 pairs/triples + uniform using OOF AUROC on the training folds only; shrinking 0.5 toward uniform limits the selection overfitting. No test labels are touched, but the selected weights are still fit on data the outer harness also scores, so a small optimistic bias in the CV loss is plausible.

description: Standardize molecules (largest fragment plus neutralization, with fallback), then replace the equal-weight rank average of RF, LightGBM, CatBoost, Tanimoto kNN (k=15) and MLP with weights chosen by scaffold-grouped inner 5-fold OOF AUROC over corners, equal pairs/triples and the uniform blend, shrunk halfway toward uniform.

Weight each training molecule by 1/sqrt(count of its Murcko scaffold in the training set, normalized to mean 1) and pass these as sample_weight to the RF, LightGBM and CatBoost fits, leaving features, hyperparameters and rank averaging unchanged.
